texts.preamble: Mrs. Bincy Philip --/-- vs Ravi Sharma on 3 August, 2023 In The Court Of Harvinder Singh, Presiding Officer : Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-01, (West), Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi. Award/Judgment
texts.facts: Vide this judgment/award, this Tribunal shall decide claim of compensation on account of injuries sustained by injured Bincy Philip in a road vehicular accident which took place on 23.10.2015 at about 1:10 AM at Tax Barier, Near Prem Dhaba, PS Sadar Rupnagar, Punjab. CASE OF PETITIONER SIDE 2. Succinctly, the case put forward by petition/DAR is that on 23.10.2015 injured Bincy Philip along with other persons were going on a tour to Manali in a hired Tempo Traveler bearing registration No. DL-1VA-8948 which was being driven by Kamal Garg. At about 1:10 AM, their vehicle reached at Tax Barier, Near Prem Dhaba, P.S. Sadar Rupnagar, Punjab. A Truck bearing Mrs. Bincy Philip --/-- vs Ravi Sharma on 3 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158132046/ 3 registration No. HP69A7149 was parked in the middle of the road in rash and negligent manner without any indication or parking lights or reflector in the complete darkness at that place. Due to same, their vehicle bearing registration No. DL1VA8948 struck against said vehicle No. HP69A7149. As a consequence, all the occupants of tempo traveler sustained various injuries. Driver/Kamal Garg and Mrs Maya Abraham died due to same. The incident happened solely due to rash and negligent driving/parking of respondent no.01 who has wrongly parked his vehicle in the middle of the road without any indicators/reflectors. Injured was working at Employees State Insurance Hospital and was getting a salary of Rs.64,659/- per month at the time of incident. The respondent no.01 being driver, the respondent no.02 being owner and respondent no.03 being the insurer of offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner(s). [MACT No.477649/2016 ] Page No.4 of 29 HARVINDER by HARVINDER SINGH SINGH Date: 2023.08.04 16:37:16 +0530 applicant(s)/claimant(s) has/have sought compensation of Rs.31,25,000/- (Rupees Thirty One Lakhs Twenty Five Thousand Only) from the respondents. MISCELLANEOUS PROCEEDINGS 3. Notice of the application/petition/DAR was issued to the respondents on which they appeared and filed their WS(s)/reply(ies) to the present petition/application. RESPONSE OF RESPONDENT NO.01 &02 4. In gist, the response of the respondent no.01 & 02 as discernible from their reply/written statement is that the respondent no.1 was having a valid driving licence to drive truck bearing registration No. HP69A7149 at the time of incident. Vehicle in question was duly insured with the respondent No.3 covering the date of accident. There was no negligence on the part of the respondent no.1. One set of rear tyres of their vehicle has brusted and its excel has also broken down. Respondent no.1 has parked their vehicle to the left side of the road. Respondent no.1 took all safety measures by giving regular hazardous light. He also put some grass and bricks near the truck so that the other commuters can make out that their vehicle is parked in breakdown condition. Deceased driver of the vehicle bearing no. DL-1VA-8948 was driving at a very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and hit their vehicle from behind. Incident took place due to the sole negligence of the deceased driver of the vehicle bearing no. DL-1VA-8948. With these averments, respondent no. 1 &2 have prayed for dismissal of the same. RESPONSE OF RESPONDENT NO.03 5. In gist, the response of the respondent no.03 as discernible from its reply/written statement is that Incident in Bincy Philip Vs. Ravi Sharma & Ors. ] Page No.5 of 29 HARVINDER SINGH SINGH Date: 2023.08.04 16:37:25 +0530 question took place due to the sole negligence of the deceased who was the driver of vehicle bearing registration No. DL1VA- 8948(Tempo Traveler). Vehicle bearing registration No. HP69A7149 (HGV-Truck) was insured with it vide policy no. 42103/31/15/630002778 for period 03.08.2015 to 02.08.2016 in the name of Sh. Shankar Ram. With these main contentions, respondent No.3 prayed for dismissal of the present petition. ISSUES 6.1 following issues on 27.07.2017:- 1. Whether the injured Bincy Philip suffered injuries in the accident that took place on 22.10.2015 at about 01:10 Am at Tax Barrier, near Prem Dhaba, PS Sadar Rupnagar, Punjab due to rash and negligent driving/parking of vehicle i.e. truck bearing registration number HR69A7149 due to wrongful act or negligence of respondent no.1 Ravi Sharma, who was driving the vehicle? OPP 3. Relief. 6.2 Thereafter, matter was fixed for evidence of petitioner side. PETITIONER SIDE EVIDENCE 7.1 The petitioner/claimant examined herself as PW1 to establish her claim. She tendered her evidence by way of affidavit Ex.PW1/A reiterating and supporting the contents of their application/petition. She relied upon the documents i.e.copy of FIR Mark A, copy of insurance policy Mark D, copy of DL of Bincy Philip Vs. Ravi Sharma & Ors. [MACT No.477649/2016] Page No.6 of 29 HARVINDER HARVINDER SINGH SINGH Date: 2023.08.04 16:37:34 +0530 driver Mark E, copy of RC Mark F, copy of her I Card Mark G, copy of salary slip for the month of February, 2016 Mark H, copy of her PAN Card and copy of income tax return for assessment year 2015-16 Mark I, copy of her Aadhar Card Ex.PW1/J, copy of TDS certificate Mark J, copy of original medical prescription Mark K, copy of bill no. 232 dated 30.10.201, the original bill No. 238 dated 30.11.2015, original bill No. 246 dated 30.12.2015, original bill no. 252 dated 30.01.2016, original bill no. 262 dated 29.02.2016, original bill no. 266 dated 31.03.2016 and original bill no. 270 dated 08.04.2016 Ex.PW1/L in her evidence. PW1 was cross-examined at length by Ld. Counsels for the respondent side which is not reproduced herein for sake of brevity and was discharged. 7.2 No other witness was examined by petitioner side, petitioner side evidence was closed vide order dated 27.11.2021 and thereafter, matter was fixed for respondent side evidence. RESPONDENT SIDE EVIDENCE 8.1 The respondent no.01 examined himself as R1W1 in connected MACT Petition No. 476356/2016 in case "Santosh vs. Ravi Sharma & ors", and same was ordered to be read in present matter also vide orders dated 02.06.2022. He in gist vide affidavit of evidence Ex.R1W1/A deposed that there was no negligence on his part. He has parked the vehicle on the left side of road and adopted all safely measures like giving regular hazardous light, putting some grass and bricks near the truck so that the other commuters should come to know that the vehicle is parked in breakdown condition. Mrs. Bincy Philip --/-- vs Ravi Sharma on 3 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158132046/ 5 Driver of the vehicle bearing no. DL-1VA-8948 was driving it at Bincy Philip Vs. Ravi Sharma & Ors. [MACT No.477649/2016] Page No.7 of 29 HARVINDER HARVINDER SINGH SINGH Date: 2023.08.04 16:37:40 +0530 a very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and hit their vehicle in question from behind. R1W1 relied upon the documents i.e. copy of RC Ex.R1W1/1; copy of permit Ex.R1W1/2; copy of his driving license Ex.R1W1/3 and copy of insurance policy Ex.R1W1/4 in his evidence. R1W1 was cross- examined by petitioner side and was discharged. 8.2 The respondent no.02 examined himself as R2W1 in connected MACT Petition No. 476356/2016 in case "Santosh vs. Ravi Sharma & ors" and same was ordered to be read in present matter also vide orders dated 02.06.2022. He in gist vide affidavit of evidence Ex.R2W1/A deposed that there was no negligence on part of respondent no.1. Respondent no.1 parked the vehicle on the left side of road and adopted all safely measures like, giving regular hazardous light, putting some grass and bricks near the truck so that the other commuters should come to know that the vehicle is parked in breakdown condition. Driver of the vehicle bearing no. DL- 1VA-8948 was driving it at a very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and hit their vehicle in question from behind. R1W1 was cross-examined by petitioner side and was discharged. 8.3 Respondent no.03 examined ASI Khushal Singh of PS City Ropar, District Ropar, Punjab as R3W1 who in gist, has deposed that he was not the IO of the case arising out of FIR No. 112 in question dated 23.10.2015. He was only assisting the IO in the said case. They received information about the accident from the Civil Hospital, Ropar District Roop Nagar, Punjab at around 12:00 noon on 23.10.2015. He accompanied IO ASI Sarabjeet to Bincy Philip Vs. Ravi Sharma & Ors. ] Page No.8 of 29 HARVINDER HARVINDER SINGH SINGH Date: 2023.08.04 16:37:46 +0530 the Civil Hospital, Ropar where they recorded the statement of Ms. Reena Raju pertaining to the accident. They reached at the spot of accident at about 4:00 PM after getting conducted the post mortem of two deceased/victims of the incident. They found both vehicles in accidental condition. He saw that two rear tyres of the right side of the truck has brusted. The truck was standing on the right side of the road. The Tempo Traveller was strucked beneath the back side of the truck. IO seized both the vehicles. He identified his statements dated 05.08.2016 and 22.02.2017 as Ex. R3W1/1. He also identified the site plan of the place of accident as Ex.R3W1/2 in his evidence. R3W1 was cross- examined by Ld.Counsel for the petitioner side, by Ld. Counsel for respondent no1. & 2 and was discharged. The injured was working as Staff Nurse at ESIC Hospital and was getting a salary of Rs.64,659/- per month at the time of incident. Submissions/contentions of the respondent no.01 and 02 are that deceased driver of the vehicle bearing no. DL- 1VA-8948 was himself driving his vehicle at a very high speed, in a rash manner and negligent manner. Submissions/contentions of the respondent no.03 are that the petitioner/claimant has failed to prove that incident took place due to rash and negligent parking of vehicle in question by respondent no.01. The incident happened due to rash and negligent driving of deceased driver of Tempo Traveler, therefore, they are not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner(s), hence, petition be dismissed. It is submitted that at least there is contributory negligence on part of deceased driver of Tempo Traveler.
texts.arguments: 11.2 Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in its division bench decision in matter of "Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Ors." (2011) 1 SCC 343 has held : - "General principles relating to compensation in injury cases 4. The provision of The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ('Act' for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. (see for example, the decisions of this court in Arvind Kumar Mishra v. New India Assurance Co.Ltd. - 2010(10) SCALE 298 and Yadava Kumar v. D.M., National Insurance Co. Ltd. - 2010 (8) SCALE 567). 9.
